source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 1 (ISLB A1) · lesson 10. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: The five duties that hold Islam up like a strong building

learn.en: Islam is like a strong building held up by five pillars: the main duties of every Muslim.
learn.title: Five pillars

learn.en: 1. Shahadah: saying and believing there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger.
learn.title: Shahadah

learn.en: 2. Salah: praying five times every day — our direct connection with Allah.
learn.title: Salah

learn.en: 3. Zakah: Muslims who have enough money give part of it to the poor and needy.
learn.title: Zakah

learn.en: 4. Sawm: fasting in the month of Ramadan.
learn.title: Sawm

learn.en: 5. Hajj: visiting the Ka'bah in Makkah once in your life, if you are able.
learn.title: Hajj

learn.en: A Muslim obeys Allah in everything, easy or hard. The pillars are how we show our faith every day.
learn.title: What is a Muslim?

order.en: Put the five pillars in order

quiz.en: How many times a day do Muslims pray?

opts: Giving part of your money to the poor and needy
Eating a big meal with friends

quiz.en: In which month do Muslims fast?
True or false? Hajj is a journey to visit the Ka'bah at least once in life, if you are able.
True or false? A Muslim is someone who only obeys Allah when it is easy.

think.q: You have savings in your piggy bank and you see a family with no warm clothes for winter. Which pillar teaches us to help?
think.a: Zakah — sharing our money with the poor. Sharing makes both families happy!

parents.summary: The five pillars: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm (Ramadan) and Hajj.

try.en: The pillars of Islam are five

parents.tip: Count the five pillars on his fingers and let him explain each one.
